source.title: Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses SAE universality and reports cross-seed SAE-transfer results, but it does not test whether SAE reconstruction errors are linearly predictable, scale predictably across SAE sizes, affect model loss in the specified way, contain the proposed two components, carry function, or result from SAE-training artifacts.
record.gate_note: The paper measures SAE reconstruction explained variance when transferring an SAE across seeds or checkpoints, and after Procrustes rotation; these are related to SAE reconstruction error but do not measure any listed claim version. Decoder-cosine, feature-firing, and steering results are not error-structure tests. Rows below record the related reconstruction measurements only and are linked to versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs only to test cross-seed and cross-checkpoint transfer of SAE dictionaries, which it explains by a residual-stream rotation. It never measures the structure of the within-model SAE error: no linear prediction of the error, no per-token error-norm scaling across SAE sizes, no loss under spliced reconstructions versus random errors, no error decomposition, no circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term, and no architecture comparison. It does not cite the dark-matter paper. Its negative EVs come from applying one seed's SAE to another seed's activations, not from SAE error on the training model.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that independently trained transformers share function up to a Haar-random orthogonal rotation of the residual basis. Decoder-cosine universality hides encoder non-transfer, and a single Procrustes rotation restores SAE reconstruction and informs steering transfer. They draw no conclusions about SAE dark matter.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains SAEs at ×8 and ×32 expansion and measures cross-seed/checkpoint reconstruction transfer, including after Procrustes alignment. It does not use the original dark-matter error decomposition or test per-token error predictability and scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with site and SAE expansion; cross-seed versus cross-checkpoint transfer differs; the toy setup distinguishes shared-I/O Cohort A from independent-init Cohort B. The paper reports ranges across sites or pairs rather than a full per-condition breakdown for several SAE results.

fits_no_version.finding: Applying one seed's SAE to another seed's activations gives negative EV at internal sites. A single-batch Procrustes rotation restores EV to near the within-seed ceiling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-seed SAE reconstruction failure is due to residual-basis rotation, and orthogonal alignment restores reconstruction.

fits_no_version.finding: A Gaussian-noise baseline matched in mean and covariance reconstructs better than naive cross-seed SAE application on the toy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Naive cross-seed SAE transfer can reconstruct worse than a matched Gaussian baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-checkpoint SAE reconstruction improves after rotation, both on the toy and on Pythia-70m (one checkpoint pair, one layer).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal alignment improves SAE transfer between checkpoints of the same training run.

record.problems: The SAE results are about cross-seed and cross-checkpoint transfer, not the dark-matter claim versions. Several values are reported only as aggregates or ranges across sites and pairs. The paper itself states that frontier-scale replication remains untested.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for decoder-cosine, feature-firing correlation, or steering results: they do not measure SAE reconstruction error or any behavior specified by the claim versions. Other site-specific SAE values are not individually stated in the text.

untested.parts: All: no regression of the SAE error on the input activation.
All: no per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes. The x8 versus x32 comparison concerns cross-seed transfer only.
All: no downstream-loss comparison of SAE-spliced versus random-error-perturbed activations.
All: no split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
All: no circuit or steering analysis with versus without the SAE error term. Steering uses diff-of-means vectors, not SAE features.
All: a single ReLU+L1 SAE architecture. No comparison of training objectives or architectures on error size.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is closest to 'discusses' only in a loose sense: the paper uses SAEs and reconstruction EV but never discusses or cites SAE dark matter or reconstruction-error structure. 'cites_only' does not fit because the original is not cited. All rows correctly link to none.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Does not test per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, or whether error persists with scale.
Does not compare model loss from SAE-reconstructed activations with loss from random errors of the same size.
Does not decompose SAE error into linearly predictable and nonlinear parts or test their proposed interpretations.
Does not test whether analyses or interventions lose model behavior when the SAE error term is omitted.
Does not test whether SAE-training choices cause dark matter or whether alternative architectures or end-to-end training reduce it.

rows.operation_detail: Applied the seed-0-trained SAE to activations from other Cohort A seeds and measured explained variance.

rows.baseline: within-seed self-EV; exact value not stated
rows.value: Cross-seed EV matches self-EV to four decimal places.
rows.note: This is a cross-seed SAE-transfer result, not a measurement of the error properties specified in the claim.

rows.subject: 104k-parameter two-layer Dyck-3 transformer (Cohort A)

rows.note: Reports rotation-corrected cross-seed transfer, not the claimed error-structure measures.

rows.subject: EleutherAI/pythia-70m-seed1
